title: Edmund and the Protocol
premise: Freya Okonkwo, caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has spent ten years hauling cargo through contested orbits, loyal to the Provision that keeps her station alive. When a deep-space ship returns with its crew aged backward, she discovers they carry a message proving the war's founding protocol was a lie — and Edmund, the ship's AI, chooses her to deliver it. Pursued by both fleets and betrayed by her own handler, Freya must decide whether loyalty to the people who raised her outweighs the truth that could free them all. In the end she broadcasts the message from the seed vault itself, ending the war at the cost of the vault — and choosing a future with Edmund over the duty that defined her.
about_author: Casper Amberdale is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they grow heirloom tomatoes and insist the best science fiction is about maintenance, not explosions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Shelves
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Establishes her decade of solitary cargo runs between the seed vault and Provision stations, her quiet bond with the vault's aging systems, and the war's grinding toll on supply lines. When the ship Meridian returns unannounced — its crew biologically twenty years younger — her routine shatters. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by wonder and immediate suspicion.

chapters.title: Edmund Speaks
chapters.summary: Alternating Freya and Edmund POVs. The Meridian's AI, Edmund, reveals the crew were de-aged by experimental stasis and that he holds a recorded confession: the war began on a falsified protocol. He asks Freya to carry it to the neutral relay. Her Provision handler, Dain, orders her to surrender the ship. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, terrifying weight of being chosen and trusted.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, intercut with fleet chatter. The run to the relay becomes a gauntlet as both fleets converge; Dain betrays her position, forcing her to jettison cargo and burn reserves. A boarding action nearly takes the message, and Edmund sacrifices his core shielding to save her. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into betrayal, love crystallizing under fire.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Were For
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, climax and resolution. Cornered at the vault, she broadcasts the confession on every channel, using the vault's antenna array — knowing the transmission will draw fire that destroys the shelves she tended for ten years. The fleets stand down as the truth spreads. In the wreckage, Edmund's voice persists in her ship's systems. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging; love chosen over duty.
